scopeReview: IMP-5.A.1–3: pollution/salinization, land-cover/hydrologic change, desertification and conservation; terraces, irrigation, shifting cultivation, wetland drainage and pastoral management; economic purpose, workloads and social consequences. Practices evaluated conditionally without stereotypes or universal effects.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli:salt-mass budget, sediment trial bars, original before/after wetland plan and group time accounts. Deterministic checks balance salt, calculate80% erosion reduction, verify ditch/outlet geometry and sum changed workloads. Additional cases examine recovery, grazing, conversion tradeoffs and social-evidence limits.
repetitionReview: Salt mass is distinct from water-volume accounts; sediment percentages from yield; before/after panels from adjacent-property maps; workload expansion from earlier equal-total time allocation. No copied or numeric-only clone. Varied keys and complete option reasoning; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: FAO irrigation/drainage and UNCCD primary definitions checked; no technical treatment prescription, actual field statistics, third-party diagram or question copied. All quantitative and map data hypothetical; student resources unchanged and no human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Stored salt increases by 70 tonnes, creating a salinization risk if the imbalance persists.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed100−30=70 tonnes retained. Distinguished salt mass from water volume; no assumption that all irrigation is harmful, no exact soil concentration from unspecified soil mass, and no crop threshold invented.
Independently calculated(40−8)/40=.8. Kept sediment units t/ha and percent distinct. Chart does not show yield or total runoff volume, so those are not inferred; no technical terrace design advice.

questions.correctOption: Additional cropland may come with reduced wetland storage or habitat functions, requiring assessment beyond crop area alone.
questions.independentReview: Checked distinct before/after polygons, right-panel drainage arrow to an outlet, and supplied storage/habitat notes. No hydrologic flood magnitude or universal ecosystem outcome inferred from an illustrative plan. Ditch label is placed along the upper vertical segment to avoid the outlet label; flow direction and the downstream outlet remain unchanged. Desktop inspection moved the outlet farther below the crop boundary to keep its text clear of that line; the ditch remains directed toward the outlet.

questions.correctOption: Women’s paid work rises by 4 hours and total listed work rises from 9 to 13 hours, while unpaid work stays 6 hours.
questions.independentReview: Independently summed women9→13, men7→9; paid women3→7, unpaid6→6. Distinct from earlier equal-total time-allocation cases: this records an increased combined burden. Group averages for one fictional community, not universal gender roles.

questions.correctOption: Shorter, less steep surface-flow paths can slow runoff and reduce its capacity to move soil.
questions.independentReview: Verified the conditional physical mechanism, avoiding a design recommendation or guaranteed conservation result. Separates erosion control from a quantitative yield claim.

questions.correctOption: Reduced recovery time can weaken vegetation regrowth and soil-fertility restoration under those conditions.
questions.independentReview: Checked that no universal safe fallow length or stereotype about a named community is given. Conditional impact of reduced recovery distinguishes management change from condemnation of an entire farming system.

questions.correctOption: A semiarid grazing area experiences sustained losses of vegetation and soil productivity under combined climatic stress and damaging land use.
questions.independentReview: Checked against UNCCD Article1:arid, semiarid and dry-subhumid degradation, not the spread of all natural deserts or hyperaridity itself. No invented erosion threshold or single-factor attribution.

questions.correctOption: Pastoral mobility by itself proves that all herding causes identical permanent degradation.
questions.independentReview: Avoided equating extensive/pastoral/nomadic systems with automatic overgrazing. Correct option is explicitly the claim to avoid; other options remain qualified evidence-based statements.

questions.correctOption: Crop output and returns alongside habitat, carbon-storage, soil and water changes.
questions.independentReview: No quantified carbon emission, actual forest claim or automatic causal estimate assigned. The question selects an assessment scope rather than declaring all forest conversion identical.

questions.correctOption: Compare soil/water benefits, crop opportunity costs, maintenance and affected groups rather than use one indicator alone.
questions.independentReview: Assessed tradeoffs without recommending a technical buffer width or claiming benefit-cost magnitudes that were not supplied. No paid policy decision or real farm intervention.

questions.correctOption: Every household member must now have greater decision-making power and a more varied diet.
questions.independentReview: Aligned IMP-5.A.3 social consequences while withholding unsupported causal or universal conclusions. No actual community or gender-income statistic invented.
